text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Catholic church is no enemy of freedom but moral order is needed to practice freedom, John Paul II has preached during his current visit to Poland which began on Saturday.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Cenal shipyard in Gdansk, which rents facilities from the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard, will build a ferry for a Norway-based shipowner to carry up to 300 passengers, 17 trailers of 24 tonnes each and 75 passenger cars, the yard said.
- The Polska Zegluga Baltycka (PZB) shipping firm has launched a new daily connection linking Gdansk, northern Poland, and Nynashamn, southern Sweden, PZB said.
- Estonian state railways have lost 18 million Estonian crowns on the Warsaw-Tallinn line in 1996 and the connection may be discontinued this year, the Estonian company said.

- Curtis Electronics and Curtis Market in Mlawa, north-eastern Poland, will lay off 120 out of 613 employees of the two firms. The redundancies will not affect Curtis' disabled employees, the companies said.

- The Tymbark juice processing firm, controlled by the Progress National Investment Fund (NFI) No 11 needs 15 million zlotys to fund facility development as production capacity does not allow Tymbark to meet market demand. Tymbark hopes the Fund will supply the capital, Tymbark's president Julian Pawlak said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The first session of trading in commodity options will start at the Warsaw Commodity Exchange today, exchange officials said.

- KGHM Polska Miedz copper conglomerate will launch its privatisation's advertising campaign today in nationwide media including television, radio and newspapers. The campaign has been produced by the ITI McCann-Ericson advertising agency.
- Austria's Alfred Wall AG will invest 13 million zlotys in construction of a cardboard packaging plant to employ 100 workers in Klaj, Krakow province.
- The sales of Cinquecento, Fiat 126 and Daewoo Tico accounted for 28 percent of Poland's passenger car sales in 1996, a report by the Samar car market monitoring agency said.

- The listed Bank Slaski's results in the first quarter of 1997 were disappointing and the bank's net profit in the period showed a 38 percent decline compared with the same period last year, a report by Merrill Lynch investment bank said.

- Poland's banks have reported a growing number of bad debts accrued by retail lenders. The debts' growth has been noticeable but its rate is not worrying, Kredyt Bank's spokesperson Marcin Olkowicz said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The average daily listening time of the private Radio Zet FM broadcaster's audience grew from 23 minutes in the first quarter of 1996 to 46 minutes in the first quarter of this year, a survey by the SMG/KRC market research firm said.
ZYCIE
- Poland's budget revenues will reach 128.547 billion zlotys in 1998, the finance ministry said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
